title: Semantic Drift Lighthouse: Eval harness for automated batch/cache config changes
creator: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:
Implement a lightweight, statistically-grounded evaluation harness ("Lighthouse") that runs automatically as part of the batching/caching recommender pipeline. The harness will detect semantic drift and quality regressions introduced by cost-driven config changes and produce binary accept/reject decisions plus human-review flags.

Why: automated cost optimizations (microbatching, prefix prefetch, KV cache policies) can reduce token cost but occasionally change model outputs in subtle, customer-visible ways. Existing probe suites focus on anchoring specific prompts; Lighthouse aims to provide continuous, model- and workload-aware signals with explicit statistical decisioning and an operational playbook for safe apply/rollback.

Scope / goals:
- Build a modular harness that can be invoked during shadow/canary runs and pre-apply checks for config recommendations from the autotuner.
- Produce a Lighthouse scorecard combining multiple signals (semantic similarity, hallucination proxy, behavioral fingerprint distance, length/format drift, latency/regression) into a single pass/fail and a severity bucket.
- Use non-inferiority hypothesis testing (one-sided) for semantic similarity with predefined delta margins; power the tests to control false positives while keeping sample sizes practical.
- Stratify evaluation across customer persona buckets (short-chat, long-context, instruction-following, code) and across seed prompt families.
- Wire alerts and a one-click rollback button in Redwood Console and surface scorecards in Optimize recommendations.

Signals and metrics (examples):
- SemSim: sentence-embedding cosine mean (SBERT/SimCSE baseline) and change in mean similarity.
- Hallucination proxy: classifier+heuristics on presence of hallucinated entities (normalized rate).
- Behavioral fingerprint: KL divergence over token unigram distributions and n-gram novelty score relative to baseline.
- Structural drift: distribution shift in output length, stop-token rates, and function-calling schema adherence.
- Latency and error rate deltas.

Decisioning rules (examples):
- Non-inferiority test on SemSim with delta = -0.03 (allow up to 3% drop); pass if lower bound of 95% CI is above delta and p-value < 0.01.
- Immediate fail if hallucination rate increases by >1.5x AND absolute increase >0.5 percentage points.
- Fail if behavioral fingerprint KL increases beyond threshold derived from historical variance (top 1% tail).
- If signals disagree, escalate to human-in-the-loop review with a priority score computed from weighted signals.

Sampling and human review plan:
- Default sample size per canary: 1,000 paired prompts stratified across personas. For low-traffic/expensive models, use 250 paired prompts plus conservative thresholds.
- Automated triage picks 1% random + 5% targeted (cases that triggered borderline signals) for human review. Human reviewers use a compact rubric (correctness, fidelity, hallucination, formatting).

Telemetry / dashboards / ops:
- Lighthouse scorecard stored per-config-change with versioned artifacts (input prompt set hash, seed list, baseline model id, config diff).
- Console dashboard: per-model drift heatmap, recent failing config diffs, and historical trend lines for SemSim and hallucination rate.
- Alerts: slack + PagerDuty for P0 regressions (semantic drop + hallucination spike). Non-critical failures go to an ops queue for product review.

Rollback playbook (high level):
- Auto-rollback triggers: binary fail on canary + severity bucket >= high -> automatic revert of config.
- Soft-fail: block auto-apply, notify PM/SE, surface one-click rollback and recommended mitigation (reduce batch size, disable certain cache layers).
- Post-rollback: run forensics harness to produce a minimal repro that demonstrates the regression and attach to incident.

Integration points:
- Recommender (autotuner) to call Lighthouse in shadow mode and before apply.
- Console + Optimize to display scorecards and provide rollback controls.
- Evals infra to manage golden prompt families and maintain seed corpora per persona.

Deliverables:
- Lighthouse service (lightweight microservice) and REST contract used by autotuner and console.
- Stratified seed corpora and tooling to generate paired comparisons.
- Acceptance/rollback playbook doc and console UI components.
- Unit + integration tests and a first run on two candidate models and three config families.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Statistical thresholds may be brittle for low-signal workloads; we mitigate with persona stratification and conservative non-inferiority margins.
- Added pre-apply latency for large sample sizes; mitigate via shadow runs and sampling heuristics.

Success criteria (high level):
- Lighthouse detects at least 90% of seeded regressions in synthetic tests and keeps false positive rate under 2% in historical replay.
- No customer-facing regressions attributable to autotuner changes in first 3 months of rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Lighthouse service returns pass/fail + signal breakdown for a given config diff and seed set within acceptable runtime (< 10 minutes for 1k samples).
Non-inferiority testing implemented for SemSim with configurable delta and confidence levels; unit tests for statistical correctness included.
Console shows per-config Lighthouse scorecard and exposes a one-click rollback that reverts the applied config and annotates the event with the scorecard id.
Autotuner blocks auto-apply when Lighthouse returns fail or when severity >= high; shadow mode runs recorded for all recommendations.
Human review flow exists: triage queue, compact rubric, and 1-click incident creation with attached Lighthouse artifacts.
test_plan: Synthetic regression suite: inject known perturbations (prompt paraphrase, token masking, prefix trimming) and verify Lighthouse flags failures.
Replay historical config changes from last 12 months against archived telemetry to measure false positive rate and detection sensitivity.
Canary rollout: run Lighthouse in shadow then limited canary (5% traffic) for three config families and validate no customer regressions.
A/B human review: compare automated triage labels vs. blinded human rubric on 500 paired outputs to calibrate severity weighting.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (shadow-only): run Lighthouse on all autotuner recs for 2 weeks and collect metrics (no blocking).
Phase 2 (canary-protect): block auto-apply for any rec that fails Lighthouse; run canary apply for approved recs (5% traffic).
Phase 3 (auto-block+alert): enable blocking and automatic rollback for high-severity failures; integrate with PagerDuty alerts.
Post-launch (iterative): tune thresholds based on observed false positives and add new signal types as needed.

2025-02-22 - Marco Li: Implemented initial SBERT baseline and paired sampling harness. Found high variance on short-chat persona — reducing sample size increases noise.
2025-02-26 - Research (note): Ran synthetic perturbation where prefix trimming reduced SemSim mean by 3.8% and Lighthouse flagged as fail under current thresholds.
2025-03-01 - Marco Li: Prototype REST endpoint live in dev. Started wiring scorecard into a Console dev dashboard. Need design input for triage UI (pinging @Design).
